The decision tree algorithm, one of the most common algorithms in practice, is a predictive model. Its users don’t need to be technical, as it is easy to interpret and explain. Decision tree is an algorithm that allows data sets to be split into smaller data sets, and consists of internal nodes that determines the split criteria and leaf nodes where the results are represented.

LDA, an algorithm that assumes that all classes can be separated linearly, is used to distinguish classes by maximizing the distance between two classes. Aiming to project the original data matrix into a lower dimensional area, LDA is one of the most common methods used in dimension reduction.

It is a probability-based classifier that assumes that each feature is independent from each other. Since there are no associated features, it performs well even in high-dimensional data sets. Parameters for each term can be learned separately and the processing speed is high.

KNN, which is frequently used in artificial intelligence and biomedical signal analysis, performs the classification process by comparing the test data with the training data. KNN is applied to an unknown set searches for the nearest k training set in its n-dimensional space. The closest k values are calculated using distance measurements. Although it is a simple approach, it has a robust theoretical structure and can outperform much more complex methods.
